d: To establish Braxtone Advisory as a trusted, high-growth regional partner to insurance-sector boards, executive teams, regulators and investors by developing commercially relevant propositions, winning and expanding strategic client relationships, and consistently delivering measurable outcomes.
A. Business Strategy, P&L and Growth
Define and execute the Advisory business strategy, annual business plan and three-year growth roadmap in alignment with the Group’s priorities.
Own the practice P&L, including revenue, gross margin, utilization, headcount, operating costs, working capital and collections.
Build a focused portfolio of repeatable, high-value offerings and determine where Braxtone should lead, partner or use external specialists.
Translate market opportunities into a disciplined pipeline, account plans and achievable sales and delivery forecasts.
Prepare regular performance reports and recommendations for the Group CEO and Executive Committee.
B. Business Development and Client Origination
Originate and convert new assignments through personal market credibility, executive relationships, referrals, partnerships and targeted campaigns.
Develop trusted relationships with board members, CEOs, C-suite executives, regulators, investors and other senior stakeholders across the GCC.
Lead client discovery, opportunity qualification, proposal development, commercial structuring, pricing, negotiation and contracting.
Grow key accounts through structured relationship plans, cross-selling and the identification of follow-on opportunities.
Maintain clear pipeline discipline, including probability-weighted forecasting, next actions, ownership and conversion analysis.
C. Client Leadership and Delivery Excellence
Act as executive sponsor for strategic engagements and remain accountable for outcomes, quality, client confidence and commercial performance.
Convert complex client issues into clear hypotheses, workplans, governance arrangements, decision papers and implementable recommendations.
Establish rigorous engagement controls covering scope, milestones, budget, resourcing, risks, dependencies, change requests and billing.
Ensure that deliverables meet leading consulting standards and are practical, evidence-based and tailored to the GCC insurance environment.
Intervene early where engagements are at risk, resolve escalations professionally and capture lessons learned
D. Service Portfolio and Intellectual Capital

Develop and lead offerings across insurance strategy and growth, operating-model and performance transformation, claims and profitability improvement, regulatory and licensing advisory, governance and risk, digital and AI-enabled transformation, M&A and post-merger integration, restructuring and run-off, and feasibility and business planning.
Create methodologies, diagnostic tools, proposal assets, case studies and quality standards that improve differentiation and delivery efficiency.
Produce relevant thought leadership and represent Braxtone at selected industry forums, roundtables, webinars and media opportunities.
Maintain current knowledge of insurance-market developments, regulatory change, emerging technologies and competitor activity across the region.
Design the target organization and resource model for the practice, balancing senior client leadership, core delivery capability and specialist expertise.
Recruit, coach and retain a high-performing team with clear objectives, development plans, succession coverage and performance accountability.
Build scalable delivery capacity, including effective use of India-based or other offshore resources where appropriate, while protecting quality and client confidentiality.
Create a collaborative, inclusive and high-integrity culture that combines commercial ambition with professional judgement and accountability.
Ensure appropriate utilization, workload management, knowledge sharing and continuing professional development
F. Governance, Risk and Group Collaboration
Apply robust engagement acceptance, conflict, independence, confidentiality, data-protection, subcontractor and quality-review controls.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulatory requirements, Group policies and contractual obligations in each market.
Work closely with Braxtone’s Insurance, Claims, Assistance and Digital businesses to create integrated solutions without compromising advisory objectivity.
Build and manage a reliable network of subject-matter experts, alliance partners and subcontractors, with clear accountability for quality and economics.
Corporate and business-unit strategy, market entry, distribution, product and portfolio strategy, customer value propositions
Target operating models, process redesign, cost and performance improvement, change management and implementation support
Claims transformation, leakage and recovery reviews, loss-ratio improvement, underwriting and technical operations
Commercial and operational due diligence, M&A support, post-merger integration, restructuring, run-off and market exit
Licensing, regulatory remediation, governance, risk, compliance and board/executive advisory
Digital strategy, automation, data and analytics, AI use cases, InsurTech partnerships and technology-enabled operating change
Detailed annual targets will be agreed with the Group CEO and Executive Committee. Performance will be assessed through a balanced scorecard covering the following outcomes:
Revenue, gross margin, collections, utilization and performance against approved budget
Qualified pipeline, proposal conversion, new strategic accounts, account expansion and strength of senior relationships
Client satisfaction, repeat business, referenceability, measurable engagement outcomes and effective escalation management
Milestone and budget performance, quality-review results, scope control and risk management
Priority offerings launched, reusable intellectual capital, alliances and market visibility
Critical hires, retention, capability development, succession, engagement and productive deployment of the team
Compliance with engagement acceptance, conflict, confidentiality, contracting, data-protection and quality requirements
Complete a fact-based review of the existing Advisory portfolio, pipeline, delivery model, capabilities and economics; agree the strategic priorities and operating model.
Present and secure approval for a three-year practice plan, annual budget, market and account priorities, service portfolio, talent plan and delivery model.
Build a qualified opportunity pipeline and establish a consistent cadence for account management, proposals, forecasting and collections.
Strengthen governance and quality controls across all active engagements and implement a clear project and portfolio reporting framework.
Win and successfully mobilize priority assignments that demonstrate Braxtone’s differentiated insurance expertise and create referenceable outcomes.
Recruit or deploy the critical leadership and delivery capabilities required to execute the approved plan, including scalable offshore support where appropriate.
q: Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, insurance, engineering or another relevant discipline; a master’s degree or MBA is preferred.

Relevant professional credentials—such as ACII, FCII, CPCU, actuarial qualifications, CFA, CPA/CA, CISA, PMP or recognised change/transformation certification—are advantageous where relevant to the candidate’s specialism.
Typically 15+ years of relevant professional experience, including substantial experience in management consulting or advisory and at least five years in senior leadership roles.

Current or recent experience at Director, Executive Director or equivalent level in a Big Four firm, recognized management consultancy, specialist insurance advisory business or comparable professional-services organization is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated insurance-sector depth across one or more of general insurance, life and health, takaful, reinsurance, broking or claims, supported by a broad understanding of the insurance value chain.
Strong knowledge of GCC insurance markets and regulatory environments; a credible regional executive network and prior GCC/MENA consulting experience are highly desirable.
Proven record of personally originating and converting material advisory engagements, growing key accounts and managing a profitable portfolio or practice.
Track record of leading complex, multi-workstream engagements from diagnosis through implementation, with board and C-suite exposure.

d: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are hiring a Senior Site Reliability / Gitops Engineer to our Information Systems (IS) team. This role is an opportunity for an “automation-first” senior technologist with a passion for Linux to build a career with Canonical and drive the success with those leveraging Ubuntu and open source products. If you have experience of IT operations automation, Infrastructure as Code and a passion for technology, then you will enjoy working with some of the best people in the industry at Canonical.
The IS team at Canonical supports and maintains all of Canonical’s IT production services. The team is in charge of running services used by over 60 million Ubuntu users.

As an Senior SRE & Gitops engineer you’ll be in a unique position to drive operations automation to the next level, both in our own private clouds as well as in the public clouds. We do this by utilizing the best of open source infrastructure as code software, software development practices such as CI/CD pipelines, and Canonical’s leading products for software operation automation.

In addition to defining the infrastructure as code, you will improve Canonical products and the open-source technologies they’re based on by providing critical feedback to developers on how their products operate at scale. This is done by submitting bugs (and sometimes writing pull requests) and collaborating on design and implementations with other teams within the company.
You’ll be part of a global team of SREs that work together and support each other to provide the best possible services to our company, Canonical’s customers and the Ubuntu Community.
r: Drive the development of automation, Gitops in your team as an embedded tech lead
Closely collaborate with the IS architect to align your solutions with the IS architecture vision
Design and architect services that IS can offer to the organization as products
Apply your experience of IaC to develop infrastructure as code practice within IS by constantly increasing automation and improving IaC processes
Automate software operations for re-usability and consistency across private and public clouds, taking into consideration the complexities of distributed systems
Maintain operational responsibility for all of Canonical’s core services, networks, and infrastructure

Develop skills in troubleshooting, capacity planning, and performance investigation, Setting up, maintaining and using observability tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, and Elasticsearch; design, implement and maintain monitoring and alerting for various systems and services
Provide assistance and work with globally distributed engineering, operations, and support peers
Be given uninterrupted development time to focus on larger projects and automation of manual tasks
Share your experience, know-how and best practices with other team members in design sessions, mentorship and ‘doing work together’
Carry final responsibility for time-critical escalations
What we are looking for in you
A modern view on hosting architecture, driven by infrastructure as code across both private and public clouds.
A product mindset thriving to develop products rather than solutions.
Python software development experience, with large projects
Experience working with Kubernetes or other container orchestration systems.
Proven exposure to manage and deploy cloud infrastructure with code.
Practical knowledge of Linux networking, routing, and firewalls
Affinity with various forms of Linux storage, from Ceph to Databases
Hands-on experience administering enterprise Linux servers
Extensive knowledge of cloud computing concepts and technologies
Bachelor's degree or greater, preferably in computer science or related engineering field
Able to communicate clearly and effectively in English over email, chat, video or voice calls and in-person
Motivated and able to troubleshoot from kernel to web, and willing to ask others when appropriate
A willingness to be flexible and able to learn new things quickly
Be inspired by the needs of fast-changing environments
Happy to work within distributed teams
Be passionate and familiarized about open-source, especially Ubuntu or Debian

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.
Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform
Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
